newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Soft in thin talks amid weak swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Soft in thin talks amid weak swaps.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market softened in thin talks amid weak swaps quotes but players were optimistic of imminent buying from China, traders said on Tuesday.
"Supplies are pretty sufficient at the moment...not many cargoes are going out of Singapore and some are still coming from the Middle East," said an independent.
Two cargoes would arrive Singapore from the Middle East and Venezuela in February and one more is coming in March, adding supplies to the market, traders said.
Fuel oil swaps quotes slid from Monday's levels, with March swaps quoted at $102.75/$103.50 per tonne compared with $104.00/$104.5.
The market traded on Tuesday at $103.00 per tonne compared to Monday's 104.50 trade.
Chinese buyers, who are expected to re-enter the market after the early-Febuary Chinese Lunar New Year holidays, continued to stay away from the market.
"Traditionally there is still no working mood even one or two weeks after the new year holidays," said a Chinese trader.
Enquiries from China should emerge in late February or early March, the trader said.
Concerns over scheduled maintenance turnarounds of two refineries in Singapore in March, which could tighten supplies, eased slightly, traders said.
Mobil 280,000-bpd refinery will be shut down for six weeks starting March 15 and Singapore Refining Co's refinery will shut an 18,000-bpd hydrocracker unit from March 2-22.
In the LSWR market, talks were thin and buying interest was seen at $20.75 per barrel.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
